summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, epilepsy, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for a persistent productive cough. A chest X-ray revealed a new right mid/lower lung opacity suggestive of pneumonia, and he was treated with a course of levofloxacin adjusted for renal function. His cough improved during the hospital stay, and he remained stable without fever or respiratory distress. Due to financial barriers, his stroke prevention regimen was transitioned from Aggrenox to aspirin and clopidogrel. A foot ulcer and fungal infection were identified, and he was started on topical miconazole. He was discharged home with instructions to complete his antibiotic, monitor weight, and follow up with his care team.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Bronchitis, not specified as acute or chronic
Ulcer of other part of foot
